title: The Category of Each Member in the Store
constraints: visit_id is unique in Purchases and always appears in Visits
reference:
WITH member_stats AS (
  SELECT
    m.member_id,
    m.name,
    COUNT(v.visit_id) AS visits,
    COUNT(p.visit_id) AS purchases
  FROM Members AS m
  LEFT JOIN Visits AS v
    ON v.member_id = m.member_id
  LEFT JOIN Purchases AS p
    ON p.visit_id = v.visit_id
  GROUP BY m.member_id, m.name
)
SELECT
  member_id,
  name,
  CASE
    WHEN visits = 0 THEN 'Bronze'
    WHEN 100 * purchases / visits >= 80 THEN 'Diamond'
    WHEN 100 * purchases / visits >= 50 THEN 'Gold'
    ELSE 'Silver'
  END AS category
FROM member_stats;
brute:
SELECT m.member_id, m.name, 'Bronze' AS category
FROM Members AS m
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Visits AS v WHERE v.member_id = m.member_id)
UNION ALL
SELECT member_id, name,
  IF(5 * bought >= 4 * visited, 'Diamond', IF(2 * bought >= visited, 'Gold', 'Silver'))
FROM (
  SELECT m.member_id, m.name,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Visits AS v WHERE v.member_id = m.member_id) AS visited,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Purchases AS p
     WHERE p.visit_id IN (SELECT v.visit_id FROM Visits AS v WHERE v.member_id = m.member_id)) AS bought
  FROM Members AS m
) AS counted
WHERE visited > 0
notes:
## Intuition

Each member needs two counts: how many visits they made and how many of those visits ended in a purchase. Joining `Members` to `Visits` to `Purchases` with **left joins** keeps every member and every visit, and counting the non-null ids on each side gives both numbers in one `GROUP BY`. A `CASE` then turns the counts into a category, checking "no visits" first so the division never sees a zero.

## Approach

1. `member_stats`: start from `Members` (`m`), left join their visits (`v`) and each visit's purchase (`p`). Group by member; `COUNT(v.visit_id)` is the number of visits and `COUNT(p.visit_id)` the number that ended in a purchase.
2. The outer `SELECT` maps the counts to a category: `'Bronze'` when `visits = 0`, otherwise compare `100 * purchases / visits` with 80 and then 50, falling through to `'Silver'`.

## Example 1, step by step

| member_id | name | visits | purchases | rate | category |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 9 | Alice | 2 (18, 21) | 1 (18) | 50 | Gold |
| 11 | Bob | 3 (22, 16, 12) | 1 (12) | 33.33 | Silver |
| 3 | Winston | 1 (19) | 0 | 0 | Silver |
| 8 | Hercy | 1 (17) | 1 (17) | 100 | Diamond |
| 1 | Narihan | 0 | 0 | none | Bronze |

## Complexity

- Time: O(M + V + P) with hashed joins on `member_id` and `visit_id`, for M members, V visits and P purchases.
- Space: O(M) for one counted row per member.

## Pitfalls

- An inner join to `Visits` drops members who never visited, so no one is ever `'Bronze'`.
- `COUNT(*)` counts the single null-padded row of a visitless member as a visit, making them `'Silver'` instead of `'Bronze'`.
- A member who visited but never bought has rate 0 and is `'Silver'`, not `'Bronze'`.
- The thresholds are inclusive: exactly 80 is `'Diamond'` and exactly 50 is `'Gold'`.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `m` | `Members`, the table every output row comes from |
| `v` | the member's visits, or `null` when they have none |
| `p` | the purchase made on visit `v`, or `null` |
| `member_stats` | one row per member with `visits` and `purchases` |
| `category` | the tier picked by the `CASE` |

narration.1: The member_stats CTE counts visits and purchases for every member.
narration.5: COUNT of the visit id skips the null row of a member with no visits, so such a member gets 0.
narration.6: COUNT of the purchase id counts only the visits that matched a purchase.
narration.7: Members is the left-most table, so every member keeps a row.
narration.8: A left join attaches each of the member's visits, keeping members who never came.
narration.10: A second left join attaches the purchase made on each visit, if any.
narration.12: Grouping by member collapses their visits into one row of counts.
narration.18: A member with no visits is Bronze; testing this first keeps the division below from dividing by zero.
narration.19: A conversion rate of at least 80 is Diamond.
narration.20: Otherwise a rate of at least 50 is Gold, and anything lower falls through to Silver.
